clue.text: Joint that is nearly suggestive ?

explanation.surface: A question about whether some joint is a little risqué.
explanation.walkthrough: A risqué remark is said to be 'near the knuckle', so a word that is 'nearly suggestive' is, cryptically, the joint itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A finger joint is a knuckle, and 'near the knuckle' is the idiom for slightly indecent humour.

clue.text: Great Warlord at the range

explanation.surface: A famous military leader at the shooting range.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Kitchener was Britain's War Secretary in the Great War; a kitchener is also an old name for a kitchen range or its cook.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Kitchener led Britain's War Office in 1914; the word also means a cooking stove.

clue.text: Wild mad tune!

indicators.note: wild tells us the letters of mad tune run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a frenzied piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Untamed means wild and unrestrained, as a crazy melody is.

clue.text: Kipling book's about fabulous king-artist — weigh it with these

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the others

parts.note: Kim is a novel by Rudyard Kipling
King Log is the do-nothing ruler of the frogs in Aesop's fable
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A Kipling novel features a legendary royal painter.
explanation.walkthrough: King Log is the idle log the gods gave the frogs as their king in Aesop's fable, hence 'fabulous'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kilograms are metric units of weight, so things are weighed in them.

clue.text: Place of exile of the Spanish scholar

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a scholar

explanation.surface: Where a Spanish academic was banished.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon was banished to this Mediterranean island in 1814.

clue.text: A cloak for an unhealthy-looking kid …

parts.note: someone unhealthy-looking is pale, wan of face
a kid is a small child, a tot

explanation.surface: A coat to wrap round a sickly-looking child.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots carry the sense into the next clue, where the child reappears.
explanation.definitionFit: A paletot is a loose outer coat or cloak, an old-fashioned garment.

clue.text: Better for the egg-producer

explanation.surface: Someone who wagers on the hen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' is one who bets; a bookmaker who lays odds is a layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookmaker lays bets, and a hen lays eggs.

clue.text: Men in the wrong can cause suffering

indicators.note: in places the first-named word inside the next one

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Men who are in the wrong can make others suffer.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment is severe pain or anguish.

clue.text: They are characteristic of letters in the press

explanation.surface: Describing what typifies printed letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Types are typical examples of a class; in printing, pieces of metal bearing letters.

clue.text: … who makes up the full amount with a pound

parts.note: the word who points back to the kid of the previous clue, a small child or tot
L is the abbreviation for pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: The child from the previous clue makes up the sum with a pound coin.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots join this clue to 5 across: 'who' stands for the kid there, so it gives TOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A total is the whole sum, everything added together.

clue.text: Hidden explosive to catch a gannet?

parts.note: the booby is a tropical seabird of the gannet family
to trap is to catch

explanation.surface: A concealed bomb as a device for catching seabirds.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a booby is a bird related to the gannet, so the trap is read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A booby trap is a concealed explosive set to go off when disturbed.

clue.text: Hail a wise man with reverence

parts.note: ho is a call used to hail someone or draw attention
a mage is a magus, a wise man or sorcerer

explanation.surface: Greeting a sage respectfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Homage is respect or honour shown publicly, the same as deep regard.

clue.text: The House of Commons is so unequalled

definitions.text: The House of Commons is so

explanation.surface: A boast that the lower chamber has no equal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Commons has no peers in it (they sit in the Lords), so it is 'without peers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no peers means having no equals, so it is matchless; and the Commons literally contains no members of the peerage.

clue.text: Mint coin worthy of a king

parts.note: a penny is a coin
royal means fit for a king

explanation.surface: A newly struck coin fit for a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mint' looks like the verb or the adjective for a new coin; it is the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Pennyroyal is a species of herb in the same family as peppermint.

clue.text: It's wrong to stray on the turbulent Ouse

parts.note: to err is to stray from the right path

indicators.note: turbulent tells us the letters of Ouse are churned up

explanation.surface: It is a mistake to drift on a rough English river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: Erroneous means mistaken, incorrect.

clue.text: December morning, on the Nore written up in old tales

parts.note: am, ante meridiem, means morning

indicators.note: written up in a down entry means the word Nore is written backwards

parts.note: the Nore is a sandbank in the Thames estuary

explanation.surface: A winter morning beside the Thames estuary recorded in old stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Boccaccio's Decameron is a fourteenth-century collection of a hundred stories.

clue.text: Safe driving capacity

parts.note: describes the instinct a motorist needs to drive without danger

explanation.definitionFit: Road sense is the awareness of traffic and hazards that keeps a driver safe.

clue.text: I've a right to dream, anyhow, of a lover

indicators.note: anyhow says the letters are put together in any order

parts.note: I've is read as I having, so the letter I with what follows

explanation.surface: Someone who dreams of a sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyhow' mixes I, R and DREAM; 'a' joins I and R.
explanation.definitionFit: An admirer is a suitor, someone who courts another.

clue.text: What's left in the barrel? Ice-cream?

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Asking what remains at the bottom of a barrel of ice-cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is a remnant, something surviving from the past.

clue.text: Like the Latin verse of an 11th century pope

explanation.surface: Describing poetry in the style of a medieval pontiff.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonine verse is Latin verse with internal rhyme; the word also means relating to a pope named Leo, such as Leo IX.

clue.text: Sweet product of French sea-artist

parts.note: de is French for of
mer is French for sea, the word French colouring this too
ARA is Associate of the Royal Academy, an artist

explanation.surface: A confection made by a French marine painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' turns both 'of' and 'sea' into French: DE MER.
explanation.definitionFit: Demerara is a brown cane sugar, a sweetening product named after a region of Guyana.

clue.text: Wing of the Italian army

parts.note: del is Italian for of the
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

explanation.surface: A flank of Italy's military.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wing' looks military; it is the triangular aircraft wing.
explanation.definitionFit: A delta wing is a triangular aircraft wing.

clue.text: Birmingham vulgarly disturbed over a dance

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters are shaken up

parts.note: Brum is the colloquial name for the English city of Birmingham

explanation.surface: Unrest in a Midlands city ahead of a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Grass in class.?

explanation.surface: A pupil telling tales at school.
explanation.walkthrough: To grass is British slang for telling the police; a 'form' is a British school class.
explanation.definitionFit: To grass is to tell on someone; being in a form means being in a school class.

clue.text: Extract a tie

explanation.surface: Taking something out, or ending level.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw is to pull out; a draw is a game ending level.

clue.text: He puts on a good show on : his day

definitions.text: He puts on a good show on : his day

parts.words: He puts on a good show on : his day
parts.note: the ... Show is a London procession held each November for the new holder of the City office

explanation.definitionFit: The holder of the City of London's chief civic office parades in an annual pageant called his Show.

clue.text: Love to rise awkwardly from bed to make a basket

definitions.text: from bed to make a basket

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: awkwardly suggests the letters of rise are clumsily jumbled

explanation.surface: A lover struggles to get out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' is a willow bed, where the basket willow is grown, not a sleeper's bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiers are willows grown in beds whose pliant shoots are woven into baskets.

clue.text: One born to inherit, we hear, that goes flying

indicators.note: we hear tells us the words are said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: a son born to inherit is an heir male, an old legal term

explanation.surface: An heir to an estate who takes to the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmail is post carried by aircraft.

clue.text: Points back to the great railway

definitions.text: Points back to the great railway

parts.words: Points back to the great railway
parts.note: points are compass directions, and the Great ... was the famous British railway company

explanation.definitionFit: The direction of sunset gave its name to the Great Western Railway of England.
